messages:
ash (eng-runtime): Heads-up — ran a full-day profiler against prod routing 2026-03-17. Seeing a 6–10ms TTFT bump on /v1/chat/stream for mid-length prompts (60–120 tokens). Kernel time slice looks elevated compared to previous baseline. :eyes:
kevin (infra): Oof. Any particular kernel selected more often? fallback->microkernel spikes?
maria (perf): quick snapshot from the probe run: kernel_selector shows 78% main-kernel, 19% microkernel, 3% fallback. But the microkernel median kernel_time went from 1.7ms -> 6.2ms p50, p95 also up. KV-hit rate dropped ~4% on those routes.
ash-bot / perf-bot: Alert created: perf.regression.rule_3135 — "route:/v1/chat/stream TTFT p50 +8ms". See perf playbook link: https://redwood.internal/perf/3135
devon (sre): Could be KV prefetch overlap — if prefetch loses the race we see more microkernel+decode. Do we have token-level kernel attribution in the console yet? I want per-token tag: kernel_variant and kv_hit boolean.
nash-bot / perf-bot: Existing instrumentation: token_latency_breakdown = [prequeue, queue_to_kernel, kernel_exec, kv_lookup, kv_prefetch_wait, decode_postproc]. No explicit kernel_variant tag yet.
maria (perf): I put a quick trace snippet into the thread (truncated):
```
trace_id: 0x9f2b
route: /v1/chat/stream
seq: 78
steps:
  - prequeue: 0.8ms
  - queue_to_kernel: 2.1ms
  - kv_lookup: 0.2ms (miss)
  - kv_prefetch_wait: 3.7ms
  - kernel_exec: 6.1ms (microkernel)
  - decode_postproc: 0.6ms
  -> total_token: 13.5ms
```
ash-bot / perf-bot: Note: this trace sample shows KV prefetch wait dominating kernel handoff in these cases.
ash-bot / ash (eng-runtime): Is this correlated with batch size changes? We did a scheduler tweak last week.
kevin (infra): I checked the batch histograms — median batch size on that route increased from 1.9 -> 2.6 during the affected window. That could shift kernel choice heuristics in selector.
maria (perf): Hypothesis: larger microbatches + slightly degraded KV hit rate -> kernel selector favors microkernel for memory/access pattern -> microkernel kernel_exec time is higher for these seq lengths.
devon (sre): Action items:
  1) Add kernel_variant dimension to token-level metrics (string: main|micro|fallback) and kv_hit boolean.
  2) Add a TTFT vs decode breakdown heatmap per-route: x-axis token position bucket, y-axis kernel_variant, color = median TTFT.
  3) Add KV-prefetch-wait p95 alert for /v1/chat/stream at >5ms.
kevin (infra): I'll instrument kernel_variant in the selection path today. Will emit metric tag: kernel_variant and kernel_time_ms as a metric set. Also will add a short-lived sampling flag to include full trace for 1% of requests.
maria (perf): I'll build the heatmap panel in Console: group by route -> token_position_bucket -> kernel_variant; compute median TTFT and p95 decode separately. Will also add a per-route KPI card showing TTFT_p50, decode_p50, kernel_exec_p50, kv_prefetch_wait_p95. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
nash-bot / perf-bot: Sampling toggle set: kernel_variant=true for 1% sample on route /v1/chat/stream.
nash-bot / ash (eng-runtime): Can we also log the scheduler batch size at kernel handoff so we can correlate?
kevin (infra): Yes, will attach batch_size tag to the token metric. Quick example metric envelope we will emit:
```json
{"route":"/v1/chat/stream","token_pos_bucket":"50-100","kernel_variant":"micro","kv_hit":false,"batch_size":3,"kernel_time_ms":6.1,"ttft_ms":13.5}
```
maria (perf): For dashboard delta, propose a temporary overlay showing last-24h vs baseline-7d. If we see the pattern only during certain hours it might be load schedule related.
devon (sre): If kernel_variant instrumentation confirms selector flip, next step is to tune selector heuristics: prefer main-kernel for batch_size<=3 for these seq lengths. But only after rollouts to validate cost/latency tradeoff.
nash-bot / perf-bot: Created convo task: infra#3135 - emit kernel_variant; perf#3135 - dashboard heatmap + KPIs; infra#3136 - attach batch_size tag.
nash-bot / ash (eng-runtime): I'll take perf#3135 validation and run a 48h probe after changes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
